'Relentless Boost' is formatted differently from every other técnica in this PDF (no Duração/Alcance/Requisito table, no explicit grau/técnica-auxiliar header) and its placement right after Player Two's 'Técnicas Auxiliares' section (Emergency Suply, Air Strike) is the only signal I have that it belongs under Player Two (m2) rather than being its own separate manifestação-like entry or an inata-style extra. Perfect Shot's crit range change to 18-20 (Tac-50 variant only) was put in criticalBonus as free text since it's conditional on weapon choice, not an unconditional crit-range change for the whole técnica — worth double-checking how criticalBonus should represent a conditional value.

I set damageParts to a placeholder 1d10 (bludgeoning, since no damage type is ever stated in the text — could plausibly be 'force'/generic instead) since the schema wants a fixed number/denomination; this needs manual correction to either a variable/scaling formula or a documented convention for 'up to Nd10' techniques. Also flags the undocumented '(ou d12 dependendo do talento de domínio de aura)' alternate-die clause, which I did not attempt to encode.

Sky Spin, Elemental Shift, Spinning Dice: each describes a 'reduction of X dice of damage' or 'grants resistance' mechanic with no attack roll, no save gating a direct effect, and no heal/temp-HP grant — these are pure passive/reactive buffs with no clean Activity shape in the documented schema (not the jjScale 'reduction' pattern either, which is about the caster giving up their OWN outgoing damage). Configured as 'utility' with cost/activation only; full mechanical text preserved in description only.

Sky Dice and Earth Dice manifestações each state 'Técnicas Comuns: N' / 'Técnicas Auxiliares: N' counts in their header line (a per-manifestação cap on how many técnicas of each grau can be attached) — there is no schema field documented for this anywhere in data-schema.md (it wasn't in the skip-list either, since that list only covers Prof./Subcategoria/per-técnica-Categoria/Ataque-Combinado/Proficiência-banner). Devour: the reaction/'Reação' requisito combined with the actual trigger described ('quando uma criatura executar uma técnica qualquer dentro do seu alcance') is consistent with a reaction activation type — used 'reaction'.

None of the técnicas explicitly say 'Aura Total', so I used the default energy.generated pool for every manifestação/técnica cost, including the two manifestações — please confirm none of these are meant to draw from Aura Total given their fairly high base costs (Sky Dice 7, Earth Dice 6).

Falling Sky's duration ('Especial' with a stated cooldown of 1 minute before it can be re-conjured) — used durationUnits 'special' with the cooldown text carried in durationValue since there's no clean 'inst + cooldown' field pairing documented; flag if a different convention exists for cooldown-gated instant effects.

No damage type is ever stated explicitly for Falling Sky's cube-burst damage (the PDF never names Cortante/Contundente/Perfurante/etc. for it) — per activity-type-rules.md's guidance not to guess an unstated damage type, I defaulted to 'bludgeoning' as a rough guess (physical impact of an exploding cube) rather than leaving it truly blank since the schema requires a types array; this should be treated as unconfirmed and called out to the user explicitly.

Hell Servant (m1): header says 'Custo: 8 Pontos de Aura' but the body text separately describes a one-time ritual costing '1 hora e 20 Pontos de Aura máxima' to actually transform a defeated creature. I set cost=8 (the header/activation cost) and left the 20-PA-máxima ritual cost as description text only, since it's a distinct one-time per-creature ritual cost, not the manifestação's per-activation cost, and there's no schema field for a second/conditional cost.

Aura Barrier técnica (Lord's Castle, m3): grants '20 Pontos de Vida para cada 5 Pontos de Aura sacrificados' to a barrier around the castle, with a variable/uncapped amount of PA sacrificed (not a fixed activation cost) and potentially by multiple creatures, not just the caster. This doesn't cleanly fit temp HP (it's a structure's HP, not a creature's) or armorPoints (no 'resistência' language, and it isn't the caster's own resource). Left as mechanicKind utility with only the 1 PA activation cost configured; the scaling HP-per-PA-sacrificed mechanic is text-only.

Lord's Castle: 'consome 1 PA de uma criatura dentro dele por minuto para se manter no ar' — a per-minute (not per-turn) PA drain paid by whichever creature is inside the castle, not necessarily the caster. This doesn't match the constantCost pattern (which is per-turn upkeep on the activator) closely enough to configure mechanically; left as description text only.

Rule Zone (m2) and Lord's Castle (m3): both are ritual/inscription-style manifestações with costs described in a mix of PA, time, and (for Lord's Castle) money/sacrificed creatures rather than a single clean activation. I set the top-level 'cost' to the PA figure stated in each header ('Custo: 8 Pontos de Aura' / 'Custo: 16 Pontos de Aura') and left the additional time/resource/sacrifice requirements as description text, per the pattern used for Hell Servant.

Time Trap and Evil League Circle and Mark of Hell all list 'Duração: Especial' (or 'Especial / Até 1 hora') in their PDF stat tables — used durationUnits:'spec' (dnd5e's special/custom duration type) rather than inventing a fixed unit, with the exact wording preserved in the description's Duração line.

Rule Zone's own range/area is a variable circle whose radius depends on inscription time (3m up to 210m) rather than a single fixed value — used rangeUnits:'spec' with the full table left in the description text rather than picking one radius to hardcode into a numeric range field.

Activation type for Hell Servant, Rule Zone, and Lord's Castle: none of these three manifestações state a specific action word (Ação, Ação Bônus, Reação, Ação de Poder) for their own top-level activation — they're all ritual/inscription processes measured in minutes/hours/days. Set activationType='special' per the 'PDF doesn't specify any particular action type' rule in activity-type-rules.md, distinct from Integration's 9-PA técnica which similarly never names an action type and also got 'special'.

Skipped the 'Prof.', 'Subcategoria' (Simbiótico/Barreira/Sacrificial), 'Ataque Combinado', and 'Proficiência do Hatsu (Ultimato)' banner per the explicit skip list, and skipped the ASPECTO INATO 'Aura Potente' section as category-wide content not hatsu-specific.

'Aura Cannon' says 'Você pode usar sua concentração para acumular aura por várias rodadas, adicionando o "Explosão Ofensiva" em cada rodada' — this references a named sub-effect ('Explosão Ofensiva') that is never defined anywhere else in the PDF (looks like a possible drafting/naming inconsistency in the source, or a fragment left over from a different technique name). Archangel is a full conjured-creature stat block (CR/HP/attacks/abilities including its own attack-roll damage, a save-gated condition, a heal-over-time ability, and a jjScale-scaling Light Execution attack: 5d10 base radiant damage scaling 1 PA per 1d10 up to 21d10). This means Light Execution's jjScale damage scaling, Light Domain's healing-over-time, and Purify's condition-removal save are NOT mechanically wired up anywhere — they exist only as readable text. Archangel's activation prerequisites (sacrificing half max aura permanently, sacrificing 28 HP per conjuration, requiring a specific Item de Nen and $10,000 of religious consumables, an 8-hour long rest if destroyed) have no schema fields — left as description text only, per the 'real actor-level mechanic with no plain Activity field' guidance.

Swords of Revealing Light's zone/swords (200 HP, CR 20 each) have no explicit stated duration for how long they persist once conjured (only Freeze's own 5-round paralysis timer and Null Field's 1-round grace period are explicit) — applied the 'creates something with no stated duration/end-condition' default of 10 minutes to the manifestação itself, per the duration-default rule. If the swords are actually meant to persist until destroyed (they do have HP/CR, which could count as a stated end-condition), 'inst' might be more correct instead — flagging since the PDF doesn't say explicitly either way.

Iron Judgment (manifestação): the core mechanic is a battlefield-wide damage counter/tracker (sums damage dealt by all creatures within 30m until it crosses a threshold equal to 60x the average party/NPC level) with no PA-cost-per-turn or attribute this system tracks natively. Iron Judgment: range is genuinely a tracking radius (30m) rather than the ability's own target range for its eventual attack — modeled as rangeUnits: 'spec' with a note; a human may want to reconsider how range should be represented here since the final attack presumably targets a creature already within or near that 30m zone, but the PDF doesn't restate a separate 'attack range' distinct from the 30m tracking radius.
Neither manifestação has any técnica beneath it in this PDF — the tecnicas array is empty by design, not an omission; all mechanical content is on the two manifestações themselves.

Iron Maiden's summoned creature's 'Iron Spear' distance attack (18m, Perfurante, damage 'igual do usuário') and 'Ataque (Base)' melee attack are pure stat-block flavor for the summoned creature, not separate hatsu técnicas of the player's own tree, so I did not create Activities for them — they're captured only as description text inside the Iron Maiden manifestação.

I left the +3d10-on-ação-de-poder variant as description text only and kept the primary activity's activationType as 'bonus' (the ação bônus is the technique's base/default form per the PDF's main sentence). Flagging for a human to decide whether a second named activity should be hand-added for the ação de poder variant.

Bleeding Out's range is 'sempre igual ao da sua visão' (always equal to your sight range) — there's no clean rangeUnits enum for 'equal to your vision', so I used rangeUnits:'self' on the manifestação itself (it doesn't target anything, it conjures equipment) and put a rangeSpecial note only on the técnica (which is the one that actually makes attack rolls at that range). activationType for Bleeding Shot: PDF says 'Ao usar uma ação bônus e 1 pulga (bala)' — mapped to 'bonus'. Also uses 1 pulga (flea) as an additional consumption/resource cost that has no clean home in the schema (a crafted-ammo resource, not PA) — left as description text only.

Perfect Recipe's '2d8 Pontos de Vida' self-sacrifice cost has no clean Activity field (it's not damage to a target, an attack, save, or heal — it's a self-paid resource cost alongside the 6 PA cost). Left as description text only; not mechanized as a damage/heal activity.

Both manifestações and the one técnica ended up as pure 'utility' activities — this PDF has no attack rolls, saving throws, or damage/healing content anywhere, so no técnica in this hatsu exercises the attack/save/damage/heal decision tree at all.
